{
 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "077d0fa8",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Welcome to the `gridops` quickstarter!\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "251b7e36",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "`gridops` is an open-source and customizable grid operations model for three major U.S. interconnections (Western, Eastern, and ERCOT). Production cost modeling in `gridops` utilizes linear DC Optimal Power Flow (DC-OPF) approximation to optimize hourly unit commitment (UC) and economic dispatch (ED) processes over a user-configurable rolling horizon."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2ce322e1",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "`gridops` was created to:\n",
    "  - Address weather and water dynamics and associated vulnerabilities in U.S. bulk power systems.\n",
    "  - Link with a wide range of hydrometeorological datasets and energy system/machine learning models to explore future uncertainty in grid operations.\n",
    "  - Analyze current and future grid stress and reliability trends under a wide range of weather conditions, generation mixes, and demand growth scenarios.\n",
    "  - Create simple and user-tailored representations of the U.S. interconnections to find a balance between model accuracy and run time to answer research questions of interest."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "496c1f7f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# An example simulation!\n",
    "Let's start using `gridops` by initilizing a simulation! First, we load the package."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "3079173d",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Package version: 1.1.0\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Import the package and check the package version\n",
    "import gridops as go\n",
    "from importlib.metadata import version\n",
    "print(f\"Package version: {version('gridops')}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2bce10d9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Next, we initialize our `Model` object where we can specify the interconnection we'd like to simulate, mathematical formulation we'd like to use, and solver we'll utilize."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "9d9f08af",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stderr",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "2026-10-29 13:06:49,805 - INFO - gridops.model - Configuration: U.S. Western Interconnection - Economic Dispatch\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Instantiate the model\n",
    "model = go.Model(\n",
    "    region=\"west\",                           # U.S. Western Interconnection\n",
    "    problem=\"linear\",                        # Linear programming (economic dispatch only)\n",
    "    solver_name=\"appsi_highs\",               # Using open-source HiGHS solver\n",
    "    solver_params={\"log_to_console\": False, \n",
    "                   \"output_flag\": False},    # Optional – preventing HiGHS from printing to console\n",
    ")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "de2b0336",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Then, we point out our example configuration file (see `gridops/data/example_config_file.yml` for a full template) and number of days we'd like to simulate to start the simulation."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "fc6fba4a",
   "metadata": {},

   "source": [
    "# Access the example configuration file\n",
    "from importlib.resources import files\n",
    "config_file_path = files(\"gridops\").joinpath(\"data/example_config_file.yml\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Changing the directory to the location of the configuration file (only needed if the paths in the config file are relative \n",
    "# to the config file's location, otherwise (i.e., absolute paths in the config file), this step would not be necessary)\n",
    "import os\n",
    "os.chdir(files(\"gridops\").joinpath(\"data\"))\n",
    "\n",
    "# Run for 2 days with a 24-hour rolling horizon\n",
    "model.run(\n",
    "    config_file=config_file_path,  # Path to the model configuration file\n",
    "    n_days=2,                      # Running for 2 days\n",
    "    horizon_hours=24,              # Optional – using default 24-hour horizon\n",
    ")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b531d492",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "# Import packages for post-processing and visualization\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "# Define the number of days and hours simulated\n",
    "total_days = 2\n",
    "total_hours = total_days*24\n",
    "\n",
    "# Read the LMP and loss of load outputs\n",
    "LMPs = pd.read_parquet(\"example_outputs/duals.parquet\")\n",
    "Loss_of_load = pd.read_parquet(\"example_outputs/slack.parquet\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Look at the first few rows of the LMPs\n",
    "LMPs.head()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "27e3e872",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 800x600 with 2 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 0 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Group model outputs to find hourly average LMP and hourly total loss of load\n",
    "grouped_prices = LMPs.groupby('Time').mean(numeric_only=True)\n",
    "grouped_outages = Loss_of_load.groupby('Time').sum(numeric_only=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Plot hourly average LMPs and hourly total loss of load for the duration of our simulation\n",
    "plt.rcParams.update({'font.size': 8})\n",
    "plt.rcParams['font.sans-serif'] = \"Arial\"\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(nrows=2, ncols=1, figsize=(8,6), sharex=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "ax[0].plot(range(1, total_hours+1), grouped_prices, color='#56B4E9', label='LMP')\n",
    "ax[1].plot(range(1, total_hours+1), grouped_outages, color='#D55E00', label='Loss of Load')\n",
    "\n",
    "ax[0].set_ylabel('Average LMP ($/MWh)', weight='bold', fontsize=10)\n",
    "ax[1].set_xlim([1,total_hours])\n",
    "ax[1].set_xticks([1, 12, 24, 36, 48])\n",
    "ax[1].set_xlabel('Hours', weight='bold', fontsize=10)\n",
    "ax[1].set_ylabel('Total Loss of Load (MWh)', weight='bold', fontsize=10)\n",
    "\n",
    "fig.legend(loc='center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.001), ncol=2)\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.show()\n",
    "plt.clf()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "6f267eee",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Finally, let's look at the generation mix results."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "52159f50",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# Read the generation output\n",
    "Generation = pd.read_parquet(\"example_outputs/mwh.parquet\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Group generation by type and time to have hourly total generation by each type\n",
    "grouped_generation = Generation.groupby(['Type','Time']).sum(numeric_only=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Create a list of unique generator types\n",
    "generation_types = Generation['Type'].unique()\n",
    "\n",
    "# Create an empty dictionary to store organized generation results\n",
    "generation_timeseries = {}\n",
    "\n",
    "# Save hourly total generation by each type in a dictionary for easier plotting\n",
    "for gen_type in generation_types:\n",
    "    generation_timeseries[gen_type] = grouped_generation.loc[gen_type].to_numpy().reshape(-1)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "08b0dff4",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 800x400 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 0 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Plot total generation by type for the duration of our simulation\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8,4))\n",
    "\n",
    "ax.stackplot(range(1, total_hours+1), generation_timeseries.values(), labels=generation_timeseries.keys(), \n",
    "             colors=['#D55E00','#949494','#000000','#CA9161','#CC78BC','#808000','#0173B2','#ECE133','#029E73'])\n",
    "ax.set_xlim([1,total_hours])\n",
    "ax.set_xticks([1, 12, 24, 36, 48])\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel('Hours', weight='bold', fontsize=10)\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel('Total Generation (MWh)', weight='bold', fontsize=10)\n",
    "\n",
    "fig.legend(loc='center left', bbox_to_anchor=(0.9, 0.5), ncol=1)\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.show()\n",
    "plt.clf()"
   ]
  },

   ],
   "source": [
    "# Display the generation mix in percentages\n",
    "Total_generation_by_type = {gen_type: generation_timeseries[gen_type].sum() for gen_type in generation_timeseries.keys()}\n",
    "Total_generation = np.sum(list(Total_generation_by_type.values()))\n",
    "\n",
    "for gen_type in generation_timeseries.keys():\n",
    "    print(f'Share of {gen_type} in generation mix is {round(Total_generation_by_type[gen_type]/Total_generation*100, 2)}%')"
   ]
  }
